hypothesis: If the human trunk has eight ribs on each side, a canonical human skeletal partonomy and a public-domain anatomical description will each enumerate eight distinct rib bones on a side, and not some other count.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. The per-side count of distinct rib ordinals is exactly 8 in every admissible source that returns a count. A source is admissible only when its labels or sentences give a contiguous series of rib ordinals from 1 through N with no gaps, or an explicit typical number of ribs on one side. Grouping classes (true rib, false rib, rib cage, set of ribs), costal cartilages, and named variants (cervical rib, lumbar rib, bifid rib, supernumerary rib) do not add an ordinal and do not remove one. Left and right, when both are present, must each equal 8. Supports only if every admissible source agrees on 8.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refutes if every admissible source gives a per-side count other than 8 and the sources agree with each other. Mixed if two admissible sources give different counts, or if left and right differ inside one source. Inconclusive with reason data-unavailable if no admissible source can be retrieved. Inconclusive with reason not-operationalizable if a source lists ribs but not as a contiguous per-side ordinal series and states no typical number.

test_contract.expected_observation: The canonical human skeleton, as recorded in the Foundational Model of Anatomy and in Gray's 1918 osteology, lists exactly eight rib bones on each side.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Those sources list a contiguous series whose length is not eight, or they state a typical number of ribs on one side other than eight.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A canonical human anatomical partonomy or a public-domain anatomical description that names individual ribs or states how many ribs are on one side. The source must be independent of Aristotle's text. Individual clinical series are admissible if a public table of rib counts is retrieved, but none is required for this registration. A partial list with gaps is not a count.
test_contract.inference_method: Count distinct rib ordinals from 1 upward that are present as bones on one side, excluding cartilages and variant classes. Compare that integer, and any explicit typical number stated in the same source, with 8. Agreement of all admissible sources on 8 supports; agreement on any other integer refutes; disagreement is mixed.

interpretation: The claim is the normal human count, eight ribs on each side, not a modern claim about the frequency of cervical or lumbar ribs. 'Ribs' are mapped to the bony ribs of the thoracic cage, not to costal cartilages and not to the classes 'true', 'false' or 'floating', which are groupings of those bones. Eight is not re-read as seven vertebrosternal ribs. The test uses the canonical body those sources describe. It does not estimate how often living people depart from that canon.
caveats: Before this file was committed, a web-search snippet of a third-party HTML copy of Gray (1918) on the ribs was visible and included a stated count. The pass and fail rules above were taken from the claim text (the count is eight, or it is not) and were not changed after that snippet. The FMA service had not been queried.
A canonical partonomy is one anatomical model, not a sample of skeletons. A count other than eight refutes the claim as a statement of normal human anatomy even if some people have eight ribs.
